noi_dung:
The State of the Fourth Dhyana Heaven

When the Chan investigator reaches the state of no self, no others, he enters the First Dhyana, also called "the Ground of Joy and Bliss Born of Separation." At this stage, the meditator smashes clinging to beings, realizing "Chan bliss as food" and feeling a joy in the Dharma replete. In this samadhi state, breathing ceases—no breathing out, no breathing in—and the meditator rejoices with a special joy. Such bliss is wondrous beyond words—in short, ordinary people never taste such bliss.

In the Second Dhyana, also called "the Ground of Joy and Bliss Born of Samadhi," the meditator feels an utmost joy and bliss. Sitting in place—neither eating nor drinking—the pulse beats no more—like one dead—yet thought remains, aware of sitting in stillness.

In the Third Dhyana's samadhi, also called "the Ground of Wondrous Bliss Apart from Joy," the meditator leaves behind Chan bliss as food, leaves behind even replete Dharma joy—realizing a subtle bliss beyond all telling, wholly inconceivable. In this state, all thoughts halt—not a thought arises. There is a saying:

When not a single thought arises, the whole appears;

When the six senses suddenly stir, it is covered by clouds.

A rough translation:

Not a thought arising, the whole appears; Six senses stirring, covered by clouds.

The Fourth Dhyana, also called "the Ground of Purity through Renouncing Thought," is a state where thoughts not only halt but are wholly cast off. Then the meditator reaches an extraordinary purity, and bliss extraordinary and wondrous. Yet the Fourth Dhyana's state remains a common beings' state—not yet realizing fruition. Never be too proud. Fruition's stage is still far—the meditator must strive investigating, keep investigating, press further still to reach the state of "the Five Heavens of No Return"—there first entering the sages' stream.

Of old, the Unlearned Bhikshu (the Unlearned Bhikshu being a Bhikshu without understanding, without study — Unlearned Bikshu), reaching this Fourth Dhyana state, mistook himself realized—and wherever he went, boasted so. Never penetrating the Buddhadharma, he spoke false words—and fell into the Uninterrupted Hells as the fruit.
